about: Verbatim excerpts from every source this guide cites, saved so each fact can be traced and re-checked. Excerpts are short; see each URL (and its archived copy, when added) for full context.

sources.title: North Atlantic Right Whales in Coastal Massachusetts: the 2025/2026 Season (July 1, 2026)

excerpts.quote: 7/01/2026 Division of Marine Fisheries North Atlantic right whales have been known to aggregate in high numbers in Cape Cod Bay in the early spring for centuries.

excerpts.quote: This past season, the first aerial survey occurred on November 3, 2025
excerpts.supports: last season's first survey flight was November 3, 2025

excerpts.supports: first right whale of last season reported from Race Point Beach by a member of the public, October 26, 2025

excerpts.quote: Cape Cod Bay, 14 individuals were sighted in December followed by a January where 39 were sighted, including 33 individuals sighted on January 10, 2025, which is the most the survey has ever sighted on a single day in January.

excerpts.quote: Visual and acoustic detections in coastal Massachusetts prompted the initiation of eight separate federal Slow Zones as these detections occurred in time and/or space when federal vessel speed zones were not active.

resolved.claim: Rare visitors: harp and hooded seals occasionally turn up too, usually between January and May
resolved.problem: The harp seal report does not call harp seals rare or occasional visitors. It says sightings and strandings off the U.S. East Coast from Maine to New Jersey have been increasing since the early 1990s, usually in January–May.
resolved.resolution: Guide wording corrected on 2026-11-08 to match the source.

resolved.claim: Rare visitors: harp and hooded seals occasionally turn up too, usually between January and May
resolved.problem: The hooded seal report does not call hooded seals rare or occasional visitors. It says they are highly migratory, with increased occurrences from Maine to Florida, usually between January and May in New England waters. (Source 2, the Center for Coastal Studies seal page, calls hooded seals 'a rare sight' in this area but is not cited here.)
resolved.resolution: Guide wording corrected on 2026-11-08 to match the source.

resolved.claim: Harassing or feeding seals is against federal law
resolved.problem: The source ties only harming or harassing to federal law ('protected by federal laws that prohibit people from harming or harassing them'). For feeding it says only 'Feeding protected marine animals is also against the law,' without naming federal law. The body's wording, 'Feeding them is against the law [13]', matches the source.
resolved.resolution: Guide wording corrected on 2026-11-08 to match the source.
